zh.summary: Palma.ai 为企业提供 AI 代理的集中治理层，通过单一连接器控制权限、执行策略并审计代理与公司系统的交互。
zh.judgment: Palma.ai 切入了企业 AI 代理规模化落地的核心瓶颈——治理与合规，其商业价值取决于能否将治理层嵌入企业现有身份与基础设施，并证明其独立于通用模型和 MCP 网关的不可替代性。
zh.replaces: 替代企业手动管理 AI 代理权限、分散的 MCP 服务器配置、缺乏审计的代理调用，以及依赖通用模型自身安全机制的做法。
zh.segment: 企业 AI 代理治理与安全，基于 MCP 标准的策略执行与审计平台。
zh.product: Palma.ai 的产品是一个企业级治理层，位于 AI 代理与工具之间，提供身份、权限、策略执行、人工审批和审计功能。它支持所有主流 AI 助手（如 Claude、ChatGPT、Copilot、Cursor 等）和 MCP 服务器，通过单一连接器交付工具和技能（Skills）。平台强调参数级策略、PII 脱敏、防篡改审计和 FinOps 成本追踪，并可在本地、VPC 或气隙环境部署。官网还提到技能（Skills）作为可版本化、扫描后分发的“剧本”，将最佳实践传递给所有代理。
zh.customer: 目标客户是拥有大量 AI 代理使用需求的大型企业，尤其是 IT 安全、合规和运维团队。付费者可能是 CISO、CIO 或平台工程负责人，痛点在于代理调用缺乏可见性、权限失控、审计困难以及合规风险。官网未披露具体客户案例或行业分布，但提到“十人到十万人”的规模，暗示其面向中大型企业。
zh.workflow: 工作流从企业现有身份提供商（如 Entra、Okta）同步用户组开始，Palma 为每个用户分配一个受治理的连接器，该连接器携带其有权使用的 MCP 服务器和技能。当用户通过任意 AI 助手发起工具调用时，请求经过 Palma 的策略层：验证身份、检查参数级策略、必要时暂停等待人工审批、脱敏敏感数据，并记录完整审计日志（包括调用者、代理、参数、结果、成本和耗时）。审计日志可离线验证并流式传输到 SIEM。技能（Skills）作为可版本化的剧本，经过扫描后通过同一连接器分发。
zh.business_model: 官网未披露具体定价或收费模式。根据产品定位，可能采用企业级订阅或按连接器/用户数收费，但无证据支持。单位经济推断：若按用户数收费，需考虑部署成本（本地/VPC）和治理复杂度；若按调用量收费，则需平衡审计存储和计算成本。目前无法确认收入模式，需等待官方披露。
zh.traction: 官网提到“十人到十万人”的规模，并展示了一些界面截图（如工具调用统计、策略状态），但未提供具体客户名称、数量或收入数据。投资方包括 D11Z Ventures、Plug and Play、Deel 等，其中 D11Z 和 Plug and Play 的合伙人以客户身份背书，称“我们不仅是投资者，也是用户”。这提供了初步采用信号，但缺乏独立验证的客户案例或留存数据。
zh.moat: Palma.ai 的壁垒在于其作为企业治理层的定位：它不绑定特定 AI 助手或模型，而是基于开放 MCP 标准，并深度集成企业身份系统（Entra、Okta）和基础设施（本地、VPC、气隙）。与通用模型自带的安全功能相比，Palma 提供参数级策略、人工审批和防篡改审计，这些是企业合规的硬需求。然而，壁垒的可持续性取决于 MCP 生态的碎片化程度以及大型云厂商是否推出类似治理层。若 MCP 标准被广泛采纳且治理需求标准化，Palma 可能面临来自平台方的竞争。
zh.funding_read: 本轮为 pre-seed 轮，金额 180 万美元（按 ECB 汇率折算约 157.7 万欧元），投资方包括 Scale Now Ventures、D11Z Ventures、Deel Ventures 和 Plug and Play Ventures。此阶段表明公司处于早期产品验证和市场切入阶段，资金可能用于产品开发、团队组建和早期客户获取。但资金用途未披露，无法确认具体分配。下一里程碑可能是获取付费企业客户、验证产品市场契合度，并建立可重复的销售流程。
zh.risks: 第一，企业治理需求可能被云厂商或 AI 助手内置功能满足，导致 Palma 的独立价值被压缩。第二，MCP 标准若未能成为企业主流，Palma 的生态赌注可能落空。第三，早期客户获取依赖投资者背书，若无法转化为独立付费客户，增长将受限。第四，部署模式（本地/VPC）可能带来高实施成本，影响单位经济。
zh.takeaway: Palma.ai 的案例表明，在 AI 代理爆发期，治理与安全可能成为企业采纳的关键瓶颈。创业者可借鉴其“不绑定模型、基于开放标准、嵌入现有身份系统”的策略，以及通过投资者作为早期客户获取反馈和信任的做法。同时，需警惕平台方竞争和标准不确定性。
zh.watch_next: 关注 Palma.ai 是否披露付费客户数量、收入或具体案例研究；观察其与主要 AI 助手和 MCP 服务器的集成深度；留意 MCP 标准的采纳进展以及云厂商是否推出竞争性治理产品。

en.summary: Palma.ai provides enterprises with a central governance layer for AI agents, controlling permissions, enforcing policies, and auditing how agents interact with company systems through a single connector.
en.judgment: Palma.ai addresses the critical bottleneck of governance and compliance in scaling enterprise AI agents; its commercial value depends on embedding the governance layer into existing enterprise identity and infrastructure, and proving its indispensability beyond generic models and MCP gateways.
en.replaces: Replaces manual management of AI agent permissions, fragmented MCP server configurations, unaudited agent calls, and reliance on generic model safety mechanisms.
en.segment: Enterprise AI agent governance and security, a policy enforcement and audit platform built on the MCP standard.
en.product: Palma.ai offers an enterprise governance layer that sits between AI agents and tools, providing identity, entitlement, policy enforcement, human approval, and audit capabilities. It supports all major AI assistants (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Cursor) and MCP servers, delivering tools and Skills through a single connector. The platform emphasizes parameter-level policies, PII redaction, tamper-evident audit, and FinOps cost tracking, and can be deployed on-prem, in VPC, or air-gapped. The website also describes Skills as versioned, scanned playbooks that distribute best practices to all agents.
en.customer: Target customers are large enterprises with significant AI agent usage, particularly IT security, compliance, and operations teams. Payers are likely CISOs, CIOs, or platform engineering leads, with pain points around lack of visibility, uncontrolled permissions, audit difficulties, and compliance risks. The website does not disclose specific customer cases or industry distribution, but mentions scale from 'ten to a hundred thousand users,' suggesting mid-to-large enterprises.
en.workflow: The workflow starts with syncing user groups from existing identity providers (e.g., Entra, Okta). Palma assigns each user a governed connector that carries the MCP servers and Skills they are entitled to. When a user initiates a tool call through any AI assistant, the request passes through Palma's policy layer: identity verification, parameter-level policy checks, pausing for human approval if needed, redacting sensitive data, and logging a complete audit trail (including caller, agent, arguments, result, cost, and duration). Audit logs are tamper-evident, verifiable offline, and stream to SIEM. Skills, as versioned playbooks, are scanned and distributed through the same connector.
en.business_model: The website does not disclose specific pricing or charging models. Based on the product positioning, it may use enterprise subscriptions or charge per connector/user, but there is no evidence. Unit economics inference: if charging per user, deployment costs (on-prem/VPC) and governance complexity must be considered; if charging per call volume, balancing audit storage and compute costs is necessary. The revenue model remains unconfirmed pending official disclosure.
en.traction: The website mentions scale from 'ten to a hundred thousand users' and shows interface screenshots (e.g., tool call statistics, policy status), but does not provide specific customer names, numbers, or revenue data. Investors include D11Z Ventures, Plug and Play, Deel, among others. Partners from D11Z and Plug and Play endorse as customers, stating 'we are not just investors, we run it ourselves.' This provides early adoption signals but lacks independently verified customer cases or retention data.
en.moat: Palma.ai's moat lies in its positioning as an enterprise governance layer: it is not tied to a specific AI assistant or model, but based on the open MCP standard and deeply integrated with enterprise identity systems (Entra, Okta) and infrastructure (on-prem, VPC, air-gapped). Compared to generic model safety features, Palma offers parameter-level policies, human approval, and tamper-evident audit—hard requirements for enterprise compliance. However, the moat's sustainability depends on the fragmentation of the MCP ecosystem and whether large cloud providers launch similar governance layers. If MCP standards are widely adopted and governance needs become standardized, Palma may face competition from platform players.
en.funding_read: This is a pre-seed round of $1.8 million (approximately €1.577 million at ECB rate), with investors including Scale Now Ventures, D11Z Ventures, Deel Ventures, and Plug and Play Ventures. This stage indicates the company is in early product validation and market entry, with funds likely for product development, team building, and early customer acquisition. However, the use of funds is undisclosed, so specific allocation cannot be confirmed. The next milestone may be acquiring paying enterprise customers, validating product-market fit, and establishing a repeatable sales process.
en.risks: First, enterprise governance needs may be met by cloud providers or built-in AI assistant features, compressing Palma's independent value. Second, if the MCP standard does not become mainstream in enterprises, Palma's ecosystem bet may fail. Third, early customer acquisition relies on investor endorsement; if it cannot convert to independent paying customers, growth will be limited. Fourth, deployment models (on-prem/VPC) may bring high implementation costs, affecting unit economics.
en.takeaway: Palma.ai's case shows that during the AI agent explosion, governance and security may become key bottlenecks for enterprise adoption. Entrepreneurs can learn from its strategy of 'not binding to models, based on open standards, embedding into existing identity systems,' and using investors as early customers for feedback and trust. At the same time, be wary of platform competition and standard uncertainty.
en.watch_next: Watch whether Palma.ai discloses paying customer numbers, revenue, or specific case studies; observe the depth of integration with major AI assistants and MCP servers; monitor the adoption progress of the MCP standard and whether cloud providers launch competitive governance products.

Common Questions Quick answers about Palma.ai's enterprise MCP platform What is Palma.ai in one sentence? Palma.ai is the enterprise governance layer for MCP — it gives every person and agent a single governed connector carrying the tools and Skills they're entitled to, enforces policies on the actual arguments of a call, pauses high-risk actions for approval, and records everything in a tamper-evident audit trail. What does MCP governance mean? Deciding which person may use which tool, with which arguments, with whose approval — and being able to prove it afterwards. MCP itself covers how a client authenticates to a server and how a tool is described and called; it does not decide which person may use which tool, hold a risky call for a human, or keep the record an auditor asks for. Palma adds that layer: one governed connector per person, assigned by identity-provider group, carrying the tools and Skills they are entitled to into whichever assistant they already use. Does my team have to set up MCP servers themselves? No. Connectors are assigned by IdP group through Entra or Okta, so a joiner gets theirs on day one and a leaver loses it the moment the group changes. Every MCP server your team approves arrives through that same connector — no per-user install, no config files, no credentials sitting on a laptop. What's a Skill, and why does it matter? A tool is a verb — "send an email". A Skill is the playbook that tells an agent when and how to use the verbs it already has: how your team actually closes the books, runs an incident review, or qualifies a lead. Skills are versioned, scanned before they're served, and scoped like any other piece of enterprise software — so your best operator's process reaches everyone else's agent. Does it work with the AI clients we already use? Yes — everything is served over MCP, so the same connector, Skills and policies follow the person into whichever assistant they open, whether that's Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Cursor or something else. Switching tools doesn't mean re-approving, re-installing or re-auditing anything. How do we prove what an agent actually did? Every tool call is attributed to the person it was done for, the agent that did it, and the application it ran in — with the arguments, result, duration and cost. The audit trail is tamper-evident and verifiable offline with your own key, so your auditor doesn't have to take our word for it, and it streams to the SIEM you already run. How is Palma.ai deployed — SaaS, on-prem, VPC? Palma.ai is designed for enterprise environments: typically VPC or on-prem, including fully air-gapped, depending on your regulatory and security needs. The MCP layer and governance plane run on your infrastructure, so sensitive business data doesn't have to move into multi-tenant SaaS. We can also host it for you if you prefer.
